In pity lost, by doubtings tossed,
    My thoughts-distracted-turn
  To Thee, the Guide I reverence most,
    That I may counsel learn:

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 2.7 My heart is overpowered by the taint of pity; my mind is confused as to duty. I ask Thee: Tell me decisively what is good for me. I am Thy disciple. Instruct me who has taken refuge in Thee.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 2.7 My heart is oppressed with pity; and my mind confused as to what my duty is. Therefore, my Lord, tell me what is best for my spiritual welfare, for I am Thy disciple. Please direct me, I pray.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 2.7 With my nature overpowered by weak commiseration, with a mind bewildered about duty, I supplicate You. Telll me for certain that which is better; I am Your disciple. Instruct me who have taken refuge in You.

records.sanskrit:
न हि प्रपश्यामि ममापनुद्याद्
यच्छोकमुच्छोषणमिन्द्रियाणाम्।
अवाप्य भूमावसपत्नमृद्धं
राज्यं सुराणामपि चाधिपत्यम् ॥
records.iast:
na hi prapaśyāmi mamāpanudyād yacchokamucchoṣaṇamindriyāṇām
avāpya bhūmāvasapatnamṛddhaṃ rājyaṃ surāṇāmapi cādhipatyam
records.speaker: Arjuna

arnold.content:
I know not what would heal the grief
    Burned into soul and sense,
  If I were earth's unchallenged chief--
    A god--and these gone thence!

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 2.8 I do not see that it would remove this sorrow that burns up my senses, even if I should attain prosperous and unrivalled dominion on earth or lordship over the gods.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 2.8 For should I attain the monarchy of the visible world, or over the invisible world, it would not drive away the anguish which is now paralysing my senses."

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 2.8 Because, I do not see that which can, even after aciring on this earth a prosperous kingdom free from enemies and even sovereignty over the gods, remove my sorrow (which is) blasting the senses.

records.sanskrit:
सञ्जय उवाच।
एवमुक्त्वा हृषीकेशं गुडाकेशः परन्तप।
न योत्स्य इति गोविन्दमुक्त्वा तूष्णीं बभूव ह ॥
records.iast:
sañjaya uvāca
evamuktvā hṛṣīkeśaṃ guḍākeśaḥ parantapaḥ
na yotsya iti govindamuktvā tūṣṇīṃ babhūva ha
records.speaker: Sanjaya

arnold.content:
Sanjaya.
  So spake Arjuna to the Lord of  Hearts,
  And sighing,"I will not fight!" held silence then.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 2.9 Sanjaya said Having spoken thus to Hrishikesha (the Lord of the senses), Arjuna (the coneror of sleep), the destroyer of foes, said to Krishna, "I will not fight" and became silent.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 2.9 Sanjaya continued: "Arjuna, the conqueror of all enemies, then told the Lord of All-Hearts that he would no fight, and became silent, O King!

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 2.9 Sanjaya said Having spoken thus to Hrsikesa (Krsna), Gudakesa (Arjuna), the afflictor of foes, verily became silent, telling Govinda, 'I shall not fight.' fight.'

records.sanskrit:
तमुवाच हृषीकेशः प्रहसन्निव भारत।
सेनयोरुभयोर्मध्ये विषीदन्तमिदं वचः ॥
records.iast:
tamuvāca hṛṣīkeśaḥ prahasanniva bhārata
senayorubhayormadhye viṣīdantamidaṃ vacaḥ
records.speaker: Sanjaya

arnold.content:
To whom, with tender smile, (O Bharata! )
  While the Prince wept despairing 'twixt those hosts,
  Krishna made answer in divinest verse:

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 2.10 To him who was despondent in the midst of the two armies, Krishna, as if smiling, O Bharata, spoke these words.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 2.10 Thereupon the Lord, with a gracious smile, addressed him who was so much depressed in the midst of the two armies.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 2.10 O descendant of Bharata, to him who was sorrowing between the two armies, Hrsikesa, mocking as it were, said these words:

records.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच।
अशोच्यानन्वशोचस्त्वं प्रज्ञावादांश्च भाषसे।
गतासूनगतासूंश्च नानुशोचन्ति पण्डिताः ॥
records.iast:
śrībhagavānuvāca
aśocyānanvaśocastvaṃ prajñāvādāṃśca bhāṣase
gatāsūnagatāsūṃśca nānuśocanti paṇḍitāḥ
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
Krishna.
  Thou grievest where no grief should be! thou speak'st
  Words lacking wisdom! for the wise in heart
  Mourn not for those that live, nor those that die.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 2.11 The Blessed Lord said Thou hast grieved for those that should not be grieved for, yet thou speakest words of wisdom. The wise grieve neither for the living nor for the dead.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 2.11 Lord Shri Krishna said: Why grieve for those for whom no grief is due, and yet profess wisdom? The wise grieve neither for the dead nor the living.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 2.11 The Blessed Lord said You grieve for whose who are not to be grieved for; and you speak words of wisdom! The learned do not grieve for the departed and those who have not departed.

records.sanskrit:
न त्वेवाहं जातु नासं न त्वं नेमे जनाधिपाः।
न चैव न भविष्यामः सर्वे वयमतः परम् ॥
records.iast:
na tvevāhaṃ jātu nāsaṃ na tvaṃ neme janādhipāḥ
na caiva na bhaviṣyāmaḥ sarve vayamataḥ param
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
Nor I, nor thou, nor any one of these,
  Ever was not, nor ever will not be,
  For ever and for ever afterwards.
  All, that doth live, lives always!

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 2.12 Nor at any time indeed was I not, nor thou, nor these rulers of men, nor verily shall we ever cease to be hereafter.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 2.12 There was never a time when I was not, nor thou, nor these princes were not; there will never be a time when we shall cease to be.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 2.12 But certainly (it is) not (a fact) that I did not exist at any time; nor you, nor these rulers of men. And surely it is not that we all shall cease to exist after this.

records.sanskrit:
देहिनोऽस्मिन्यथा देहे कौमारं यौवनं जरा।
तथा देहान्तरप्राप्तिर्धीरस्तत्र न मुह्यति ॥
records.iast:
dehino.asminyathā dehe kaumāraṃ yauvanaṃ jarā
tathā dehāntaraprāptirdhīrastatra na muhyati
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
To man's frame
  As there come infancy and youth and age,
  So come there raisings-up and layings-down
  Of other and of other life-abodes,
  Which the wise know, and fear not.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 2.13 Just as in this body the embodied (soul) passes into childhood, youth and old age, so also does it pass into another body; the firm man does not grieve thereat.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 2.13 As the soul experiences in this body infancy, youth and old age, so finally it passes into another. The wise have no delusion about this.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 2.13 As are boyhood, youth and decrepitude to an embodied being in this (present) body, similar is the acisition of another body. This being so, an intelligent person does not get deluded.

records.sanskrit:
मात्रास्पर्शास्तु कौन्तेय शीतोष्णसुखदुःखदाः।
आगमापायिनोऽनित्यास्तांस्तितिक्षस्व भारत ॥
records.iast:
mātrāsparśāstu kaunteya śītoṣṇasukhaduḥkhadāḥ
āgamāpāyino.anityāstāṃstitikṣasva bhārata
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
This that irks--
  Thy sense-life, thrilling to the elements--
  Bringing thee heat and cold, sorrows and joys,
  'Tis brief and mutable! Bear with it, Prince!
  As the wise bear.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 2.14 The contacts of the senses with the objects, O son of Kunti, which cause heat and cold, pleasure and pain, have a beginning and an end; they are impermanent; endure them bravely, O Arjuna.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 2.14 Those external relations which bring cold and heat, pain and happiness, they come and go; they are not permanent. Endure them bravely, O Prince!

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 2.14 But the contacts of the organs with the objects are the producers of cold and heat, happiness and sorrow. They have a beginning and an end, (and) are transient. Bear them, O descendant of Bharata.

records.sanskrit:
यं हि न व्यथयन्त्येते पुरुषं पुरुषर्षभ।
समदुःखसुखं धीरं सोऽमृतत्वाय कल्पते ॥
records.iast:
yaṃ hi na vyathayantyete puruṣaṃ puruṣarṣabha
samaduḥkhasukhaṃ dhīraṃ so.amṛtatvāya kalpate
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
The soul which is not moved,
  The soul that with a strong and constant calm
  Takes sorrow and takes joy indifferently,
  Lives in the life undying!

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 2.15 That firm man whom, surely, these afflict not, O chief among men, to whom pleasure and pain are the same, is fit for attaining immortality.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 2.15 The hero whose soul is unmoved by circumstance, who accepts pleasure and pain with equanimity, only he is fit for immortality.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 2.15 O (Arjuna, who are) foremost among men, verily, the person whom these do not torment, the wise man to whom sorrow and happhiness are the same he is fit for Immortality.

records.sanskrit:
नासतो विद्यते भावो नाभावो विद्यते सतः।
उभयोरपि दृष्टोऽन्तस्त्वनयोस्तत्त्वदर्शिभिः ॥
records.iast:
nāsato vidyate bhāvo nābhāvo vidyate sataḥ
ubhayorapi dṛṣṭo.antastvanayostattvadarśibhiḥ
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
That which is
  Can never cease to be; that which is not
  Will not exist. To see this truth of both
  Is theirs who part essence from accident,
  Substance from shadow.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 2.16 The unreal hath no being; there is non-being of the real; the truth about both has been seen by the knowers of the Truth (or the seers of the Essence).

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 2.16 That which is not, shall never be; that which is, shall never cease to be. To the wise, these truths are self-evident.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 2.16 Of the unreal there is no being; the real has no nonexistence. But the nature of both these, indeed, has been realized by the seers of Truth.

records.sanskrit:
अविनाशि तु तद्विद्धि येन सर्वमिदं ततम्।
विनाशमव्ययस्यास्य न कश्चित्कर्तुमर्हति ॥
records.iast:
avināśi tu tadviddhi yena sarvamidaṃ tatam
vināśamavyayasyāsya na kaścitkartumarhati
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
Indestructible,
  Learn thou! the Life is, spreading life through all;
  It cannot anywhere, by any means,
  Be anywise diminished, stayed, or changed.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 2.17 Know that to be indestructible, by Which all this is pervaded. None can cause the destruction of That, the Imperishable.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 2.17 The Spirit, which pervades all that we see, is imperishable. Nothing can destroy the Spirit.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 2.17 But know That to be indestructible by which all this is pervaded. None can bring about the destruction of this Immutable.

records.sanskrit:
अन्तवन्त इमे देहा नित्यस्योक्ताः शरीरिणः।
अनाशिनोऽप्रमेयस्य तस्माद्युध्यस्व भारत ॥
records.iast:
antavanta ime dehā nityasyoktāḥ śarīriṇaḥ
anāśino.aprameyasya tasmādyudhyasva bhārata
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
But for these fleeting frames which it informs
  With spirit deathless, endless, infinite,
  They perish. Let them perish, Prince! and fight!

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 2.18 These bodies of the embodied Self, Which is eternal, indestructible and immeasurable, are said to have an end. Therefore fight, O Arjuna.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 2.18 The material bodies which this Eternal, Indestructible, Immeasurable Spirit inhabits are all finite. Therefore fight, O Valiant Man!

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 2.18 These destructible bodies are said to belong to the everlasting, indestructible, indeterminable, embodied One. Therefore, O descendant of Bharata, join the battle.

records.sanskrit:
य एनं वेत्ति हन्तारं यश्चैनं मन्यते हतम्।
उभौ तौ न विजानीतो नायं हन्ति न हन्यते ॥
records.iast: ya enaṃ vetti hantāraṃ yaścainaṃ manyate hatam ubhau tau na vijānīto nāyaṃ hanti na hanyate
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
He who shall say, "Lo! I have slain a man!"
  He who shall think, "Lo! I am slain!" those both
  Know naught! Life cannot slay. Life is not slain!

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 2.19 He who takes the Self to be the slayer and he who thinks It is slain, neither of them ï1knowsï1. It slays not, nor is It slain.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 2.19 He who thinks that the Spirit kills, and he who thinks of It as killed, are both ignorant. The Spirit kills not, nor is It killed.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 2.19 He who thinks of this One as the killer, and he who thinks of this One as the killed both of them do not know. This One does not kill, nor is It killed.

records.sanskrit:
न जायते म्रियते वा कदाचिन्
नायं भूत्वा भविता वा न भूयः।
अजो नित्यः शाश्वतोऽयं पुराणो
न हन्यते हन्यमाने शरीरे ॥
records.iast:
na jāyate mriyate vā kadācin nāyaṃ bhūtvā bhavitā vā na bhūyaḥ
ajo nityaḥ śāśvato.ayaṃ purāṇo na hanyate hanyamāne śarīre
records.speaker: Krishna

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 2.20 It is not born, nor does It ever die; after having been, It again ceases not to be; unborn, eternal, changeless and ancient, It is not killed when the body is killed.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 2.20 It was not born; It will never die, nor once having been, can It cease to be. Unborn, Eternal, Ever-enduring, yet Most Ancient, the Spirit dies not when the body is dead.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 2.20 Never is this One born, and never does It die; nor is it that having come to exist, It will again cease to be. This One is birthless, eternal, undecaying, ancient; It is not killed when the body is killed.

records.sanskrit:
वेदाविनाशिनं नित्यं य एनमजमव्ययम्।
कथं स पुरुषः पार्थ कं घातयति हन्ति कम् ॥
records.iast:
vedāvināśinaṃ nityaṃ ya enamajamavyayam
kathaṃ sa puruṣaḥ pārtha kaṃ ghātayati hanti kam
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
Who knoweth it exhaustless, self-sustained,
  Immortal, indestructible,--shall such
  Say, "I have killed a man, or caused to kill?"

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 2.21 Whosoever knows It to be indestructible, eternal, unborn and inexhaustible, how can that man slay, O Arjuna, or cause to be slain?

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 2.21 He who knows the Spirit as Indestructible, Immortal, Unborn, Always-the-Same, how should he kill or cause to be killed?

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 2.21 O Partha, he who knows this One as indestructible, eternal, birthless and undecaying, how and whom does that person kill, or whom does he cause to be killed! [This is not a estion but only an emphatic denial.-Tr.]

records.sanskrit:
वासांसि जीर्णानि यथा विहाय
नवानि गृह्णाति नरोऽपराणि।
तथा शरीराणि विहाय जीर्णा-
न्यन्यानि संयाति नवानि देही ॥
records.iast:
vāsāṃsi jīrṇāni yathā vihāya navāni gṛhṇāti naro.aparāṇi
tathā śarīrāṇi vihāya jīrṇāni anyāni saṃyāti navāni dehī
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
Nay, but as when one layeth
    His worn-out robes away,
  And taking new ones, sayeth,
    "These will I wear to-day!"
  So putteth by the spirit
    Lightly its garb of flesh,
  And passeth to inherit
    A residence afresh.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 2.22 Just as a man casts off worn-out clothes and puts on new ones, so also the embodied Self casts off worn-out bodies and enters others which are new.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 2.22 As a man discards his threadbare robes and puts on new, so the Spirit throws off Its worn-out bodies and takes fresh ones.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 2.22 As after rejecting wornout clothes a man takes up other new ones, likewise after rejecting wornout bodies the embodied one unites with other new ones.

records.sanskrit:
नैनं छिन्दन्ति शस्त्राणि नैनं दहति पावकः।
न चैनं क्लेदयन्त्यापो न शोषयति मारुतः ॥
records.iast:
nainaṃ chindanti śastrāṇi nainaṃ dahati pāvakaḥ
na cainaṃ kledayantyāpo na śoṣayati mārutaḥ
records.speaker: Krishna

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 2.23 Weapons cut It not, fire burns It not, water wets It not, wind dries It not.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 2.23 Weapons cleave It not, fire burns It not, water drenches It not, and wind dries It not.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 2.23 Weapons do not cut It, fire does not burn It, water does not moisten It, and air does not dry It.

records.sanskrit:
अच्छेद्योऽयमदाह्योऽयमक्लेद्योऽशोष्य एव च।
नित्यः सर्वगतः स्थाणुरचलोऽयं सनातनः ॥
records.iast:
acchedyo.ayamadāhyo.ayamakledyo.aśoṣya eva ca
nityaḥ sarvagataḥ sthāṇuracalo.ayaṃ sanātanaḥ
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
Impenetrable,
  Unentered, unassailed, unharmed, untouched,
  Immortal, all-arriving, stable, sure,

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 2.24 This Self cannot be cut, burnt, wetted, nor dried up. It is eternal, all-pervading, stable, immovable and ancient.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 2.24 It is impenetrable; It can be neither drowned nor scorched nor dried. It is Eternal, All-pervading, Unchanging, Immovable and Most Ancient.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 2.24 It cannot be cut, It cannot be burnt, cannot be moistened, and surely cannot be dried up. It is eternal, omnipresent, stationary, unmoving and changeless.

records.sanskrit:
अव्यक्तोऽयमचिन्त्योऽयमविकार्योऽयमुच्यते।
तस्मादेवं विदित्वैनं नानुशोचितुमर्हसि ॥
records.iast:
avyakto.ayamacintyo.ayamavikāryo.ayamucyate
tasmādevaṃ viditvainaṃ nānuśocitumarhasi
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
Invisible, ineffable, by word
  And thought uncompassed, ever all itself,
  Thus is the Soul declared! How wilt thou, then,--
  Knowing it so,--grieve when thou shouldst not grieve?

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 2.25 This (Self) is said to be unmanifested, unthinkable and unchangeable. Therefore, knowing This to be such, thou shouldst not grieve.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 2.25 It is named the Unmanifest, the Unthinkable, the immutable. Wherefore, knowing the Spirit as such, thou hast no cause to grieve.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 2.25 It is said that This is unmanifest; This is inconceivable; This is unchangeable. Therefore, having known This thus, you ougth not to grieve.

records.sanskrit:
अथ चैनं नित्यजातं नित्यं वा मन्यसे मृतम्।
तथापि त्वं महाबाहो नैवं शोचितुमर्हसि ॥
records.iast:
atha cainaṃ nityajātaṃ nityaṃ vā manyase mṛtam
tathāpi tvaṃ mahābāho naivaṃ śocitumarhasi
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
How, if thou hearest that the man new-dead
  Is, like the man new-born, still living man--
  One same, existent Spirit--wilt thou weep?

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 2.26 But even if thou thinkest of It as being constantly born and constantly dying, even then, O mighty-armed, thou shouldst not grieve.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 2.26 Even if thou thinkest of It as constantly being born, constantly dying, even then, O Mighty Man, thou still hast no cause to grieve.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 2.26 On the other hand, if you think this One is born continually or dies constantly, even then, O mighty-armed one, you ought not to grieve thus.

records.sanskrit:
जातस्य हि ध्रुवो मृत्युर्ध्रुवं जन्म मृतस्य च।
तस्मादपरिहार्येऽर्थे न त्वं शोचितुमर्हसि ॥
records.iast:
jātasya hi dhruvo mṛtyurdhruvaṃ janma mṛtasya ca
tasmādaparihārye.arthe na tvaṃ śocitumarhasi
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
The end of birth is death; the end of death
  Is birth: this is ordained! and mournest thou,
  Chief of the stalwart arm! for what befalls
  Which could not otherwise befall?

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 2.27 For certain is death for the born, and certain is birth for the dead; therefore, over the inevitable thou shouldst not grieve.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 2.27 For death is as sure for that which is born, as birth is for that which is dead. Therefore grieve not for what is inevitable.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 2.27 For death of anyone born is certain, and of the dead (re-) birth is a certainly. Therefore you ought not to grieve over an inevitable fact.

records.sanskrit:
अव्यक्तादीनि भूतानि व्यक्तमध्यानि भारत।
अव्यक्तनिधनान्येव तत्र का परिदेवना ॥
records.iast:
avyaktādīni bhūtāni vyaktamadhyāni bhārata
avyaktanidhanānyeva tatra kā paridevanā
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
The birth
  Of living things comes unperceived; the death
  Comes unperceived; between them, beings perceive:
  What is there sorrowful herein, dear Prince?

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 2.28 Beings are unmanifested in their beginning, manifested in their middle state, O Arjuna, and unmanifested again in their end. What is there to grieve about?

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 2.28 The end and the beginning of beings are unknown. We see only the intervening formations. Then what cause is there for grief?

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 2.28 O descendant of Bharata, all beings remain unmanifest in the beginning;; they become manifest in the middle. After death they certainly become unmanifest. What lamentation can there be with regard to them?

records.sanskrit:
आश्चर्यवत्पश्यति कश्चिदेन-
माश्चर्यवद्वदति तथैव चान्यः।
आश्चर्यवच्चैनमन्यः शृणोति
श्रुत्वाप्येनं वेद न चैव कश्चित् ॥
records.iast:
āścaryavatpaśyati kaścidenam āścaryavadvadati tathaiva cānyaḥ
āścaryavaccainamanyaḥ śṛṇoti śrutvāpyenaṃ veda na caiva kaścit
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
Wonderful, wistful, to contemplate!
    Difficult, doubtful, to speak upon!
  Strange and great for tongue to relate,
    Mystical hearing for every one!
  Nor wotteth man this, what a marvel it is,
    When seeing, and saying, and hearing are done!

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 2.29 One sees This (the Self) as a wonder; another speaks of It as a wonder; another hears of It as a wonder; yet having heard, none understands It at all.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 2.29 One hears of the Spirit with surprise, another thinks It marvellous, the third listens without comprehending. Thus, though many are told about It, scarcely is there one who knows It.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 2.29 Someone visualizes It as a wonder; and similarly indeed, someone else talks of It as a wonder; and someone else hears of It as a wonder. And some one else, indeed, does not realize It even after hearing about It.

records.sanskrit:
देही नित्यमवध्योऽयं देहे सर्वस्य भारत।
तस्मात्सर्वाणि भूतानि न त्वं शोचितुमर्हसि ॥
records.iast:
dehī nityamavadhyo.ayaṃ dehe sarvasya bhārata
tasmātsarvāṇi bhūtāni na tvaṃ śocitumarhasi
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
This Life within all living things, my Prince!
  Hides beyond harm; scorn thou to suffer, then,
  For that which cannot suffer.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 2.30 This, the Indweller in the body of everyone, is ever indestructible, O Arjuna; therefore, thou shouldst not grieve for any creature.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 2.30 Be not anxious about these armies. The Spirit in man is imperishable.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 2.30 O descendant of Bharata, this embodied Self existing in everyone's body can never be killed. Therefore you ought not to grieve for all (these) beings.

records.sanskrit:
स्वधर्ममपि चावेक्ष्य न विकम्पितुमर्हसि।
धर्म्याद्धि युद्धाच्छ्रेयोऽन्यत्क्षत्रियस्य न विद्यते ॥
records.iast:
svadharmamapi cāvekṣya na vikampitumarhasi
dharmyāddhi yuddhācchreyo.anyatkṣatriyasya na vidyate
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
Do thy part!
  Be mindful of thy name, and tremble not!
  Nought better can betide a martial soul
  Than lawful war;

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 2.31 Further, having regard to thy duty, shouldst not waver, for there is nothing higher for a Kshatriya than a righteous war.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 2.31 Thou must look at thy duty. Nothing can be more welcome to a soldier than a righteous war. Therefore to waver in this resolve is unworthy, O Arjuna!

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 2.31 Even considering your own duty you should not waver, since there is nothing else better for a Ksatriya than a righteous battle.

records.sanskrit:
यदृच्छया चोपपन्नं स्वर्गद्वारमपावृतम्।
सुखिनः क्षत्रियाः पार्थ लभन्ते युद्धमीदृशम् ॥
records.iast:
yadṛcchayā copapannaṃ svargadvāramapāvṛtam
sukhinaḥ kṣatriyāḥ pārtha labhante yuddhamīdṛśam
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
happy the warrior
  To whom comes joy of battle--comes, as now,
  Glorious and fair, unsought; opening for him
  A gateway unto Heav'n.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 2.32 Happy are the Kshatriyas, O Arjuna! who are called upon to fight in such a battle that comes of itself as an open door to heaven.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 2.32 Blessed are the soldiers who find their opportunity. This opportunity has opened for thee the gates of heaven.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 2.32 O son of Partha, happy are the Ksatriyas who come across this kind of a battle, which presents itself unsought for and which is an open gate to heaven.

records.sanskrit:
अथ चेत्त्वमिमं धर्म्यं संग्रामं न करिष्यसि।
ततः स्वधर्मं कीर्तिं च हित्वा पापमवाप्स्यसि ॥
records.iast:
atha cettvamimaṃ dharmyaṃ saṃgrāmaṃ na kariṣyasi
tataḥ svadharmaṃ kīrtiṃ ca hitvā pāpamavāpsyasi
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
But, if thou shunn'st
  This honourable field--a Kshattriya--
  If, knowing thy duty and thy task, thou bidd'st
  Duty and task go by--that shall be sin!

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 2.33 But if thou wilt not fight this righteous war, then having abandoned thine own duty and fame, thou shalt incur sin.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 2.33 Refuse to fight in this righteous cause, and thou wilt be a traitor, lost to fame, incurring only sin.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 2.33 On the other hand, if you will not fight this righteous battle, then, forsaking your own duty and fame, you will incur sin.

records.sanskrit:
अकीर्तिं चापि भूतानि कथयिष्यन्ति तेऽव्ययाम्।
सम्भावितस्य चाकीर्तिर्मरणादतिरिच्यते ॥
records.iast:
akīrtiṃ cāpi bhūtāni kathayiṣyanti te.avyayām
sambhāvitasya cākīrtirmaraṇādatiricyate
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
And those to come shall speak thee infamy
  From age to age; but infamy is worse
  For men of noble blood to bear than death!

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 2.34 People, too, will recount thy everlasting dishonour; and to one who has been honoured, dishonour is worse than death.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 2.34 Men will talk forever of thy disgrace; and to the noble, dishonour is worse than death.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 2.34 People also will speak of your unending infamy. And to an honoured person infamy is worse than death.

records.sanskrit:
भयाद्रणादुपरतं मंस्यन्ते त्वां महारथाः।
येषां च त्वं बहुमतो भूत्वा यास्यसि लाघवम् ॥
records.iast:
bhayādraṇāduparataṃ maṃsyante tvāṃ mahārathāḥ
yeṣāṃ ca tvaṃ bahumato bhūtvā yāsyasi lāghavam
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
The chiefs upon their battle-chariots
  Will deem 'twas fear that drove thee from the fray.
  Of those who held thee mighty-souled the scorn
  Thou must abide,

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 2.35 The great car-warriors will think that thou hast withdrawn from the battle through fear; and thou wilt be lightly held by them who have thought much of thee.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 2.35 Great generals will think that thou hast fled from the battlefield through cowardice; though once honoured thou wilt seem despicable.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 2.35 The great chariot-riders will think of you as having desisted from the fight out of fear; and you will into disgrace before them to whom you had been estimable.

records.sanskrit:
अवाच्यवादांश्च बहून्वदिष्यन्ति तवाहिताः।
निन्दन्तस्तव सामर्थ्यं ततो दुःखतरं नु किम् ॥
records.iast:
avācyavādāṃśca bahūnvadiṣyanti tavāhitāḥ
nindantastava sāmarthyaṃ tato duḥkhataraṃ nu kim
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
while all thine enemies
  Will scatter bitter speech of thee, to mock
  The valour which thou hadst; what fate could fall
  More grievously than this?

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 2.36 Thy enemies also, cavilling at thy power, will speak many abusive words. What is more painful than this?

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 2.36 Thine enemies will spread scandal and mock at thy courage. Can anything be more humiliating?

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 2.36 And your enemies will speak many indecent words while denigrating your might. What can be more painful than that?

records.sanskrit:
हतो वा प्राप्स्यसि स्वर्गं जित्वा वा भोक्ष्यसे महीम्।
तस्मादुत्तिष्ठ कौन्तेय युद्धाय कृतनिश्चयः ॥
records.iast:
hato vā prāpsyasi svargaṃ jitvā vā bhokṣyase mahīm
tasmāduttiṣṭha kaunteya yuddhāya kṛtaniścayaḥ
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
Either--being killed--
  Thou wilt win Swarga's safety, or--alive
  And victor--thou wilt reign an earthly king.
  Therefore, arise, thou Son of Kunti! brace
  Thine arm for conflict,

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 2.37 Slain, thou wilt obtain heaven; victorious, thou wilt enjoy the earth; therefore, stand up, O son of Kunti, resolved to fight.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 2.37 If killed, thou shalt attain Heaven; if victorious, enjoy the kingdom of earth. Therefore arise, O Son of Kunti, and fight!

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 2.37 Either by being killed you will attain heaven, or by winning you will enjoy the earth. Therefore, O Arjuna, rise up with determination for fighting.

records.sanskrit:
सुखदुःखे समे कृत्वा लाभालाभौ जयाजयौ।
ततो युद्धाय युज्यस्व नैवं पापमवाप्स्यसि ॥
records.iast:
sukhaduḥkhe same kṛtvā lābhālābhau jayājayau
tato yuddhāya yujyasva naivaṃ pāpamavāpsyasi
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
nerve thy heart to meet--
  As things alike to thee--pleasure or pain,
  Profit or ruin, victory or defeat:
  So minded, gird thee to the fight, for so
  Thou shalt not sin!

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 2.38 Having made pleasure and pain, gain and loss, victory and defeat the same, engage thou in battle for the sake of battle; thus thou shalt not incur sin.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 2.38 Look upon pleasure and pain, victory and defeat, with an equal eye. Make ready for the combat, and thou shalt commit no sin.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 2.38 Treating happiness and sorrow, gain and loss, and conest and defeat with eanimity, then engage in battle. Thus you will not incur sin.

records.sanskrit:
एषा तेऽभिहिता साङ्ख्ये बुद्धिर्योगे त्विमां शृणु।
बुद्ध्या युक्तो यया पार्थ कर्मबन्धं प्रहास्यसि ॥
records.iast:
eṣā te.abhihitā sāṅkhye buddhiryoge tvimāṃ śṛṇu
buddhyā yukto yayā pārtha karmabandhaṃ prahāsyasi
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
Thus far I speak to thee
  As from the "Sankhya"--unspiritually--
  Hear now the deeper teaching of the Yog,
  Which holding, understanding, thou shalt burst
  Thy Karmabandh, the bondage of wrought deeds.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 2.39 This, which has been taught to thee, is wisdon concerning Sankhya. Now listen to wisdom concerning Yoga, endowed with which, O Arjuna, thou shalt cast off the bonds of action.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 2.39 I have told thee the philosophy of Knowledge. Now listen and I will explain the philosophy of Action, by means of which, O Arjuna, thou shalt break through the bondage of all action.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 2.39 O Partha, this wisdom has been imparted to you from the standpoint of Self-realization. But listen to this (wisdom) from the standpoint of Yoga, endowed with which wisdom you will get rid of the bondage of action.

records.sanskrit:
नेहाभिक्रमनाशोऽस्ति प्रत्यवायो न विद्यते।
स्वल्पमप्यस्य धर्मस्य त्रायते महतो भयात् ॥
records.iast:
nehābhikramanāśo.asti pratyavāyo na vidyate
svalpamapyasya dharmasya trāyate mahato bhayāt
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
Here shall no end be hindered, no hope marred,
  No loss be feared: faith--yea, a little faith--
  Shall save thee from the anguish of thy dread.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 2.40 In this there is no loss of effort, nor is there any harm (production of contrary results or transgression). Even a little of this knowledge (even a little practice of this Yoga) protects one from great fear.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 2.40 On this Path, endeavour is never wasted, nor can it ever be repressed. Even a very little of its practice protects one from great danger.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 2.40 Here there is no waste of an attempt; nor is there (any) harm. Even a little of this righteousness saves (one) from great fear.

records.sanskrit:
व्यवसायात्मिका बुद्धिरेकेह कुरुनन्दन।
बहुशाखा ह्यनन्ताश्च बुद्धयोऽव्यवसायिनाम् ॥
records.iast:
vyavasāyātmikā buddhirekeha kurunandana
bahuśākhā hyanantāśca buddhayo.avyavasāyinām
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
Here, Glory of the Kurus! shines one rule--
  One steadfast rule--while shifting souls have laws
  Many and hard.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 2.41 Here, O joy of the Kurus, there is but a single one-pointed determination; many-branched and endless are the thoughts of the irresolute.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 2.41 By its means, the straying intellect becomes steadied in the contemplation of one object only; whereas the minds of the irresolute stray into bypaths innumerable.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 2.41 O scion of the Kuru dynasty, in this there is a single, one-pointed conviction. The thoughts of the irresolute ones have many branches indeed, and are innumerable.

records.sanskrit:
यामिमां पुष्पितां वाचं प्रवदन्त्यविपश्चितः।
वेदवादरताः पार्थ नान्यदस्तीति वादिनः ॥
records.iast:
yāmimāṃ puṣpitāṃ vācaṃ pravadantyavipaścitaḥ
vedavādaratāḥ pārtha nānyadastīti vādinaḥ
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
Specious, but wrongful deem
  The speech of those ill-taught ones who extol
  The letter of their Vedas, saying, "This
  Is all we have, or need;"

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 2.42 Flowery speech is uttered by the unwise, taking pleasure in the eulogising words of the Vedas, O Arjuna, saying, "There is nothing else."

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 2.42 Only the ignorant speak in figurative language. It is they who extol the letter of the scriptures, saying, There is nothing deeper than this.'

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 2.42-2.43 O son of Prtha, those undiscerning people who utter this flowery talk which promises birth as a result of rites and duties, and is full of various special rites meant for the attainment of enjoyment and affluence , they remain engrossed in the utterances of the Vedas and declare that nothing else exists; their minds are full of desires and they have heaven as the goal.

records.sanskrit:
कामात्मानः स्वर्गपरा जन्मकर्मफलप्रदाम्।
क्रियाविशेषबहुलां भोगैश्वर्यगतिं प्रति ॥
records.iast:
kāmātmānaḥ svargaparā janmakarmaphalapradām
kriyāviśeṣabahulāṃ bhogaiśvaryagatiṃ prati
records.speaker: Krishna

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 2.43 Full of desires, having heaven as their goal, (they utter speech which is directed to ends) leading to new births as the result of their works, and prescribe various methods abounding in specific actions, for the attainment of pleasure and power.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 2.43 Consulting only their own desires, they construct their own heaven, devising arduous and complex rites to secure their own pleasure and their own power; and the only result is rebirth.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 2.42-2.43 O son of Prtha, those undiscerning people who utter this flowery talk which promises birth as a result of rites and duties, and is full of various special rites meant for the attainment of enjoyment and affluence , they remain engrossed in the utterances of the Vedas and declare that nothing else exists; their minds are full of desires and they have heaven as the goal.

records.sanskrit:
भोगैश्वर्यप्रसक्तानां तयापहृतचेतसाम्।
व्यवसायात्मिका बुद्धिः समाधौ न विधीयते ॥
records.iast:
bhogaiśvaryaprasaktānāṃ tayāpahṛtacetasām
vyavasāyātmikā buddhiḥ samādhau na vidhīyate
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
Albeit, who wealth and power do most desire
  Least fixity of soul have such, least hold
  On heavenly meditation.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 2.44 For those who are attached to pleasure and power, whose minds are drawn away by such teaching, ï1thatï1 determinate reason is not formed which is steadily bent on meditation and Samadhi (superconscious state).

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 2.44 While their minds are absorbed with ideas of power and personal enjoyment, they cannot concentrate their discrimination on one point.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 2.44 One-pointed conviction does not become established in the minds of those who delight in enjoyment and affluence, and whose intellects are carried away by that (speech).

records.sanskrit:
त्रैगुण्यविषया वेदा निस्त्रैगुण्यो भवार्जुन।
निर्द्वन्द्वो नित्यसत्त्वस्थो निर्योगक्षेम आत्मवान् ॥
records.iast:
traiguṇyaviṣayā vedā nistraiguṇyo bhavārjuna
nirdvandvo nityasattvastho niryogakṣema ātmavān
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
Much these teach,
  From Veds, concerning the "three qualities;"
  But thou, be free of the "three qualities,"
  Free of the "pairs of opposites,"[FN#2] and free
  From that sad righteousness which calculates;
  Self-ruled, Arjuna! simple, satisfied![FN#3]

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 2.45 The Vedas deal with the three attributes (of Nature); be thou above these three attributes. O Arjuna, free yourself from the pairs of opposites, and ever remain in the ality of Sattva (goodness), freed from (the thought of) acisition and preservation, and be established in the Self.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 2.45 The Vedic Scriptures tell of the three constituents of life - the Qualities. Rise above all of them, O Arjuna, above all the pairs of opposing sensations; be steady in truth, free from worldly anxieties and centered in the Self.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 2.45 O Arjuna, the Vedas [Meaning only the portion dealing with rites and duties (karma-kanda).] have the three alities as their object. You become free from worldliness, free from the pairs of duality, ever-poised in the ality of sattva, without (desire for) acisition and protection, and self-collected.

records.sanskrit:
यावानर्थ उदपाने सर्वतः सम्प्लुतोदके।
तावान्सर्वेषु वेदेषु ब्राह्मणस्य विजानतः ॥
records.iast:
yāvānartha udapāne sarvataḥ samplutodake
tāvānsarveṣu vedeṣu brāhmaṇasya vijānataḥ
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
Look! like as when a tank pours water forth
  To suit all needs, so do these Brahmans draw
  Text for all wants from tank of Holy Writ.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 2.46 To the Brahmana who has known the Self, all the Vedas are of as much use as is a reservoir of water in a place where there is a flood.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 2.46 As a man can drink water from any side of a full tank, so the skilled theologian can wrest from any scripture that which will serve his purpose.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 2.46 A Brahmana with realization has that much utility in all the Vedas as a man has in a well when there is a flood all around.

records.sanskrit:
कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन।
मा कर्मफलहेतुर्भूर्मा ते सङ्गोऽस्त्वकर्मणि ॥
records.iast:
karmaṇyevādhikāraste mā phaleṣu kadācana
mā karmaphalaheturbhūrmā te saṅgo.astvakarmaṇi
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
But thou, want not! ask not! Find full reward
  Of doing right in right! Let right deeds be
  Thy motive, not the fruit which comes from them.
  And live in action! Labour!

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 2.47 Thy right is to work only, but never with its fruits; let not the fruits of action be thy motive, nor let thy attachment be to inaction.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 2.47 But thou hast only the right to work, but none to the fruit thereof. Let not then the fruit of thy action be thy motive; nor yet be thou enamored of inaction.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 2.47 Your right is for action alone, never for the results. Do not become the agent of the results of action. May you not have any inclination for inaction.

records.sanskrit:
योगस्थः कुरु कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा धनञ्जय।
सिद्ध्यसिद्ध्योः समो भूत्वा समत्वं योग उच्यते ॥
records.iast:
yogasthaḥ kuru karmāṇi saṅgaṃ tyaktvā dhanañjaya
siddhyasiddhyoḥ samo bhūtvā samatvaṃ yoga ucyate
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
Make thine acts
  Thy piety, casting all self aside,
  Contemning gain and merit; equable
  In good or evil: equability
  Is Yog, is piety!

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 2.48 Perform action, O Arjuna, being steadfast in Yoga, abandoning attachment and balanced in success and failure. Evenness of mind is called Yoga.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 2.48 Perform all thy actions with mind concentrated on the Divine, renouncing attachment and looking upon success and failure with an equal eye. Spirituality implies equanimity.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 2.48 By being established in Yoga, O Dhananjaya (Arjuna), undertake actions, casting off attachment and remaining eipoised in success and failure. Eanimity is called Yoga.

records.sanskrit:
दूरेण ह्यवरं कर्म बुद्धियोगाद्धनञ्जय।
बुद्धौ शरणमन्विच्छ कृपणाः फलहेतवः ॥
records.iast:
dūreṇa hyavaraṃ karma buddhiyogāddhanañjaya
buddhau śaraṇamanviccha kṛpaṇāḥ phalahetavaḥ
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
Yet, the right act
  Is less, far less, than the right-thinking mind.
  Seek refuge in thy soul; have there thy heaven!
  Scorn them that follow virtue for her gifts!

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 2.49 Far lower than the Yoga of wisdon is action, O Arjuna. Seek thou refuge in wisdom; wretched are they whose motive is the fruit.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 2.49 Physical action is far inferior to an intellect concentrated on the Divine. Have recourse then to Pure Intelligence. It is only the petty-minded who work for reward.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 2.49 O Dhananjaya, indeed, action is ite inferior to the yoga of wisdom. Take resort to wisdom. Those who thirst for rewards are pitiable.

records.sanskrit:
बुद्धियुक्तो जहातीह उभे सुकृतदुष्कृते।
तस्माद्योगाय युज्यस्व योगः कर्मसु कौशलम् ॥
records.iast:
buddhiyukto jahātīha ubhe sukṛtaduṣkṛte
tasmādyogāya yujyasva yogaḥ karmasu kauśalam
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
The mind of pure devotion--even here--
  Casts equally aside good deeds and bad,
  Passing above them. Unto pure devotion
  Devote thyself: with perfect meditation
  Comes perfect act,

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 2.50 Endowed with wisdom (evenness of mind), one casts off in this life both good and evil deeds; therefore, devote thyself to Yoga; Yoga is skill in action.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 2.50 When a man attains to Pure Reason, he renounces in this world the results of good and evil alike. Cling thou to Right Action. Spirituality is the real art of living.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 2.50 Possessed of wisdom, one rejects here both virtue and vice. Therefore devote yourself to (Karma-) yoga. Yoga is skilfulness in action.

records.sanskrit:
कर्मजं बुद्धियुक्ता हि फलं त्यक्त्वा मनीषिणः।
जन्मबन्धविनिर्मुक्ताः पदं गच्छन्त्यनामयम् ॥
records.iast:
karmajaṃ buddhiyuktā hi phalaṃ tyaktvā manīṣiṇaḥ
janmabandhavinirmuktāḥ padaṃ gacchantyanāmayam
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
and the right-hearted rise--
  More certainly because they seek no gain--
  Forth from the bands of body, step by step,
  To highest seats of bliss.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 2.51 The wise, possessed of knowledge, having abandoned the fruits of their actions, and being freed from the fetters of birth, go to the place which is beyond all evil.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 2.51 The sages guided by Pure Intellect renounce the fruit of action; and, freed from the chains of rebirth, they reach the highest bliss.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 2.51 Because, those who are devoted to wisdom, (they) becoming men of Enlightenment by giving up the fruits produced by actions, reach the state beyond evils by having become freed from the bondage of birth.

records.sanskrit:
यदा ते मोहकलिलं बुद्धिर्व्यतितरिष्यति।
तदा गन्तासि निर्वेदं श्रोतव्यस्य श्रुतस्य च ॥
records.iast:
yadā te mohakalilaṃ buddhirvyatitariṣyati
tadā gantāsi nirvedaṃ śrotavyasya śrutasya ca
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
When thy firm soul
  Hath shaken off those tangled oracles
  Which ignorantly guide, then shall it soar
  To high neglect of what's denied or said,
  This way or that way, in doctrinal writ.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 2.52 When thy intellect crosses beyond the mire of delusion, then thou shalt attain to indifference as to what has been heard and what has yet to be heard.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 2.52 When thy reason has crossed the entanglements of illusion, then shalt thou become indifferent both to the philosophies thou hast heard and to those thou mayest yet hear.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 2.52 When your mind will go beyond the turbidity of delusion, then you will acire dispassion for what has to be heard and what has been heard.

records.sanskrit:
श्रुतिविप्रतिपन्ना ते यदा स्थास्यति निश्चला।
समाधावचला बुद्धिस्तदा योगमवाप्स्यसि ॥
records.iast:
śrutivipratipannā te yadā sthāsyati niścalā
samādhāvacalā buddhistadā yogamavāpsyasi
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
Troubled no longer by the priestly lore,
  Safe shall it live, and sure; steadfastly bent
  On meditation. This is Yog--and Peace!

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 2.53 When thy intellect, which is perplexed by the Veda text, which thou hast read, shall stand immovable and steady in the Self, then thou shalt attain Self-realisation.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 2.53 When the intellect, bewildered by the multiplicity of holy scripts, stands unperturbed in blissful contemplation of the Infinite, then hast thou attained Spirituality.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 2.53 When your mind that has become bewildered by hearing [S. takes the word sruti in the sense of the Vedas.-Tr.] will become unshakable and steadfast in the Self, then you will attain Yoga that arises from discrimination.

records.sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच।
स्थितप्रज्ञस्य का भाषा समाधिस्थस्य केशव।
स्थितधीः किं प्रभाषेत किमासीत व्रजेत किम् ॥
records.iast:
arjuna uvāca
sthitaprajñasya kā bhāṣā samādhisthasya keśava
sthitadhīḥ kiṃ prabhāṣeta kimāsīta vrajeta kim
records.speaker: Arjuna

arnold.content:
Arjuna.
  What is his mark who hath that steadfast heart,
  Confirmed in holy meditation? How
  Know we his speech, Kesava? Sits he, moves he
  Like other men?

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 2.54 Arjuna said What, O Krishna, is the description of him who has steady wisdom, and is merged in the superconscious state? How does one of steady wisdom speak, how does he sit, how does he walk?

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 2.54 Arjuna asked: My Lord! How can we recognise the saint who has attained Pure Intellect, who has reached this state of Bliss, and whose mind is steady? how does he talk, how does he live, and how does he act?

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 2.54 Arjuna said O kesava, what is the description of a man of steady wisdom who is Self-absorbed? How does the man of steady wisdom speak? How does he sit? How does he move about?

records.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच।
प्रजहाति यदा कामान्सर्वान्पार्थ मनोगतान्।
आत्मन्येवात्मना तुष्टः स्थितप्रज्ञस्तदोच्यते ॥
records.iast:
śrībhagavānuvāca
prajahāti yadā kāmānsarvānpārtha manogatān
ātmanyevātmanā tuṣṭaḥ sthitaprajñastadocyate
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
Krishna.
  When one, O Pritha's Son!
  Abandoning desires which shake the mind--
  Finds in his soul full comfort for his soul,
  He hath attained the Yog--that man is such!

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 2.55 The Blessed Lord said When a man completely casts off, O Arjuna, all the desires of the mind and is satisfied in the Self by the Self, then is he said to be one of steady wisdom.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 2.55 Lord Shri Krishna replied: When a man has given up the desires of his heart and is satisfied with the Self alone, be sure that he has reached the highest state.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 2.55 The Blessed said O Partha, when one fully renounces all the desires that have entered the mind, and remains satisfied in the Self alone by the Self, then he is called a man of steady wisdom.

records.sanskrit:
दुःखेष्वनुद्विग्नमनाः सुखेषु विगतस्पृहः।
वीतरागभयक्रोधः स्थितधीर्मुनिरुच्यते ॥
records.iast:
duḥkheṣvanudvignamanāḥ sukheṣu vigataspṛhaḥ
vītarāgabhayakrodhaḥ sthitadhīrmunirucyate
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
In sorrows not dejected, and in joys
  Not overjoyed; dwelling outside the stress
  Of passion, fear, and anger; fixed in calms
  Of lofty contemplation;--such an one
  Is Muni, is the Sage, the true Recluse!

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 2.56 He whose mind is not shaken by adversity, who does not hanker after pleasures, and is free from attachment, fear and anger, is called a sage of steady wisdom.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 2.56 The sage, whose mind is unruffled in suffering, whose desire is not roused by enjoyment, who is without attachment, anger or fear - take him to be one who stands at that lofty level.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 2.56 That monk is called a man of steady wisdom when his mind is unperturbed in sorrow, he is free from longing for delights, and has gone beyond attachment, fear and anger.

records.sanskrit:
यः सर्वत्रानभिस्नेहस्तत्तत्प्राप्य शुभाशुभम्।
नाभिनन्दति न द्वेष्टि तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता ॥
records.iast:
yaḥ sarvatrānabhisnehastattatprāpya śubhāśubham
nābhinandati na dveṣṭi tasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
He who to none and nowhere overbound
  By ties of flesh, takes evil things and good
  Neither desponding nor exulting, such
  Bears wisdom's plainest mark!

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 2.57 He who is everywhere without attachment, on meeting with anything good or bad, who neither rejoices not hastes, his wisdom is fixed.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 2.57 He who wherever he goes is attached to no person and to no place by ties of flesh; who accepts good and evil alike, neither welcoming the one nor shrinking from the other - take him to be one who is merged in the Infinite.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 2.57 The wisdom of that person remains established who has not attachment for anything anywhere, who neither welcomes nor rejects anything whatever good or bad when he comes across it.

records.sanskrit:
यदा संहरते चायं कूर्मोऽङ्गानीव सर्वशः।
इन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियार्थेभ्यस्तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता ॥
records.iast:
yadā saṃharate cāyaṃ kūrmo.aṅgānīva sarvaśaḥ
indriyāṇīndriyārthebhyastasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
He who shall draw
  As the wise tortoise draws its four feet safe
  Under its shield, his five frail senses back
  Under the spirit's buckler from the world
  Which else assails them, such an one, my Prince!
  Hath wisdom's mark!

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 2.58 When, like the tortoise which withdraws on all sides its limbs, he withdraws his senses from the sense-objects, then his wisdom becomes steady.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 2.58 He who can withdraw his senses from the attraction of their objects, as the tortoise draws his limbs within its shell - take it that such a one has attained Perfection.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 2.58 And when this one fully withdraws the senses from the objects of the senses, as a tortoise wholly (withdraws) the limbs, then his wisdom remains established.

records.sanskrit:
विषया विनिवर्तन्ते निराहारस्य देहिनः।
रसवर्जं रसोऽप्यस्य परं दृष्ट्वा निवर्तते ॥
records.iast:
viṣayā vinivartante nirāhārasya dehinaḥ
rasavarjaṃ raso.apyasya paraṃ dṛṣṭvā nivartate
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
Things that solicit sense
  Hold off from the self-governed; nay, it comes,
  The appetites of him who lives beyond
  Depart,--aroused no more.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 2.59 The objects of the senses turn away from the abstinent man leaving the longing (behind); but his longing also turns away on seeing the Supreme.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 2.59 The objects of sense turn from him who is abstemious. Even the relish for them is lost in him who has seen the Truth.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 2.59 The objects recede from an abstinent man, with the exception of the taste (for them). Even the taste of this person falls away after realization the Absolute.

records.sanskrit:
यततो ह्यपि कौन्तेय पुरुषस्य विपश्चितः।
इन्द्रियाणि प्रमाथीनि हरन्ति प्रसभं मनः ॥
records.iast:
yatato hyapi kaunteya puruṣasya vipaścitaḥ
indriyāṇi pramāthīni haranti prasabhaṃ manaḥ
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
Yet may it chance,
  O Son of Kunti! that a governed mind
  Shall some time feel the sense-storms sweep, and wrest
  Strong self-control by the roots.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 2.60 The turbulent senses, O Arjuna, do violently carry away the mind of a wise man though he be striving (to control them).

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 2.60 O Arjuna! The mind of him, who is trying to conquer it, is forcibly carried away in spite of his efforts, by his tumultuous senses.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 2.60 For, O son of Kunti, the turbulent organs violently snatch away the mind of an intelligent person, even while he is striving diligently.

records.sanskrit:
तानि सर्वाणि संयम्य युक्त आसीत मत्परः।
वशे हि यस्येन्द्रियाणि तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता ॥
records.iast:
tāni sarvāṇi saṃyamya yukta āsīta matparaḥ
vaśe hi yasyendriyāṇi tasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
Let him regain
  His kingdom! let him conquer this, and sit
  On Me intent. That man alone is wise
  Who keeps the mastery of himself!

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 2.61 Having restrained them all he should sit steadfast, intent on Me; his wisdom is steady whose senses are under control.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 2.61 Restraining them all, let him meditate steadfastly on Me; for who thus conquers his senses achieves perfection.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 2.61 Controlling all of them, one should remain concentrated on Me as the supreme. For, the wisdom of one whose organs are under control becomes steadfast.

records.sanskrit:
ध्यायतो विषयान्पुंसः सङ्गस्तेषूपजायते।
सङ्गात्सञ्जायते कामः कामात्क्रोधोऽभिजायते ॥
records.iast:
dhyāyato viṣayānpuṃsaḥ saṅgasteṣūpajāyate
saṅgātsañjāyate kāmaḥ kāmātkrodho.abhijāyate
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
If one
  Ponders on objects of the sense, there springs
  Attraction; from attraction grows desire,
  Desire flames to fierce passion,

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 2.62 When a man thinks of the objects, attachment for them arises; from attachment desire is born; from desire anger arises.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 2.62 When a man dwells on the objects of sense, he creates an attraction for them; attraction develops into desire, and desire breeds anger.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 2.62-2.63 In the case of a person who dwells on objects, there arises attachment for them. From attachment grows hankering, from hankering springs anger.

records.sanskrit:
क्रोधाद्भवति सम्मोहः सम्मोहात्स्मृतिविभ्रमः।
स्मृतिभ्रंशाद् बुद्धिनाशो बुद्धिनाशात्प्रणश्यति ॥
records.iast:
krodhādbhavati sammohaḥ sammohātsmṛtivibhramaḥ
smṛtibhraṃśād buddhināśo buddhināśātpraṇaśyati
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
passion breeds
  Recklessness; then the memory--all betrayed--
  Lets noble purpose go, and saps the mind,
  Till purpose, mind, and man are all undone.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 2.63 From anger comes delusion; from delusion loss of memory; from loss of memory the destruction of discrimination; from the destruction of discrimination he perishes.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 2.63 Anger induces delusion; delusion, loss of memory; through loss of memory, reason is shattered; and loss of reason leads to destruction.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 2.63 From anger follows delusion; from delusion, failure of memory; from failure of memory, the loss of understanding; from the loss of understanding, he perishes.

records.sanskrit:
रागद्वेषविमुक्तैस्तु विषयानिन्द्रियैश्चरन् | (or वियुक्तैस्तु)
आत्मवश्यैर्विधेयात्मा प्रसादमधिगच्छति ॥
records.iast:
rāgadveṣavimuktaistu viṣayānindriyaiścaran
orviyuktaistu ātmavaśyairvidheyātmā prasādamadhigacchati
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
But, if one deals with objects of the sense
  Not loving and not hating, making them
  Serve his free soul, which rests serenely lord,
  Lo! such a man comes to tranquillity;

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 2.64 But the self-controlled man, moving among the objects with the senses under restraint and free from attraction and repulsion, attains to peace.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 2.64 But the self-controlled soul, who moves amongst sense objects, free from either attachment or repulsion, he wins eternal Peace.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 2.64 But by perceiving objects with the organs that are free from attraction and repulsion, and are under his own control, the self-controlled man attains serenity.

records.sanskrit:
प्रसादे सर्वदुःखानां हानिरस्योपजायते।
प्रसन्नचेतसो ह्याशु बुद्धिः पर्यवतिष्ठते ॥
records.iast:
prasāde sarvaduḥkhānāṃ hānirasyopajāyate
prasannacetaso hyāśu buddhiḥ paryavatiṣṭhate
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
And out of that tranquillity shall rise
  The end and healing of his earthly pains,
  Since the will governed sets the soul at peace.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 2.65 In that peace all pains are destroyed; for the intellect of the tranil-minded soon becomes steady.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 2.65 Having attained Peace, he becomes free from misery; for when the mind gains peace, right discrimination follows.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 2.65 When there is serenity, there follows eradication of all his sorrows, because the wisdom of one who has a serene mind soon becomes firmly established.

records.sanskrit:
नास्ति बुद्धिरयुक्तस्य न चायुक्तस्य भावना।
न चाभावयतः शान्तिरशान्तस्य कुतः सुखम् ॥
records.iast:
nāsti buddhirayuktasya na cāyuktasya bhāvanā
na cābhāvayataḥ śāntiraśāntasya kutaḥ sukham
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
The soul of the ungoverned is not his,
  Nor hath he knowledge of himself; which lacked,
  How grows serenity? and, wanting that,
  Whence shall he hope for happiness?

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 2.66 There is no knowledge of the Self to the unsteady and to the unsteady no meditation is possible, and to the unmeditative there can be no peace, and to the man who has no peace, how can there be happiness?

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 2.66 Right discrimination is not for him who cannot concentrate. Without concentration, there cannot be meditation; he who cannot meditate must not expect peace; and without peace, how can anyone expect happiness?

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 2.66 For the unsteady there is no wisdom, and there is no meditation for the unsteady man. And for an unmeditative man there is no peace. How can there be happiness for one without peace?

records.sanskrit:
इन्द्रियाणां हि चरतां यन्मनोऽनुविधीयते।
तदस्य हरति प्रज्ञां वायुर्नावमिवाम्भसि ॥
records.iast:
indriyāṇāṃ hi caratāṃ yanmano.anuvidhīyate
tadasya harati prajñāṃ vāyurnāvamivāmbhasi
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
The mind
  That gives itself to follow shows of sense
  Seeth its helm of wisdom rent away,
  And, like a ship in waves of whirlwind, drives
  To wreck and death.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 2.67 For the mind, which follows in the wake of the wandering senses, carries away his discrimination, as the wind (carries away) a boat on the waters.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 2.67 As a ship at sea is tossed by the tempest, so the reason is carried away by the mind when preyed upon by straying senses.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 2.67 For, the mind which follows in the wake of the wandering senses, that (mind) carries away his wisdom like the mind (diverting) a boat on the waters.

records.sanskrit:
तस्माद्यस्य महाबाहो निगृहीतानि सर्वशः।
इन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियार्थेभ्यस्तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता ॥
records.iast:
tasmādyasya mahābāho nigṛhītāni sarvaśaḥ
indriyāṇīndriyārthebhyastasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
Only with him, great Prince!
  Whose senses are not swayed by things of sense--
  Only with him who holds his mastery,
  Shows wisdom perfect.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 2.68 Therefore, O mighty-armed Arjuna, his knowledge is steady whose senses are completely restrained from sense-objects.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 2.68 Therefore, O Might-in-Arms, he who keeps his senses detached from their objects - take it that his reason is purified.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 2.68 Therefore, O mighty-armed one, this wisdom becomes established whose organs in all their varieties are withdrawn from their objects.

records.sanskrit:
या निशा सर्वभूतानां तस्यां जागर्ति संयमी।
यस्यां जाग्रति भूतानि सा निशा पश्यतो मुनेः ॥
records.iast:
yā niśā sarvabhūtānāṃ tasyāṃ jāgarti saṃyamī
yasyāṃ jāgrati bhūtāni sā niśā paśyato muneḥ
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
What is midnight-gloom
  To unenlightened souls shines wakeful day
  To his clear gaze; what seems as wakeful day
  Is known for night, thick night of ignorance,
  To his true-seeing eyes. Such is the Saint!

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 2.69 That which is night to all beings, in that the self-controlled man is awake; when all beings are awake, that is night for the Muni (sage) who sees.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 2.69 The saint is awake when the world sleeps, and he ignores that for which the world lives.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 2.69 The self-restrained man keeps awake during that which is night for all creatures. That during which creatures keep awake, it is night to the seeing sage.

records.sanskrit:
आपूर्यमाणमचलप्रतिष्ठं
समुद्रमापः प्रविशन्ति यद्वत्।
तद्वत्कामा यं प्रविशन्ति सर्वे
स शान्तिमाप्नोति न कामकामी ॥
records.iast:
āpūryamāṇamacalapratiṣṭhaṃ samudramāpaḥ praviśanti yadvat
tadvatkāmā yaṃ praviśanti sarve sa śāntimāpnoti na kāmakāmī
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
And like the ocean, day by day receiving
      Floods from all lands, which never overflows
  Its boundary-line not leaping, and not leaving,
      Fed by the rivers, but unswelled by those;--

  So is the perfect one! to his soul's ocean
      The world of sense pours streams of witchery;
  They leave him as they find, without commotion,
      Taking their tribute, but remaining sea.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 2.70 He attains peace into whom all desires enter as waters enter the ocean which, filled from all sides, remains unmoved; but not the man who is full of desires.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 2.70 He attains Peace, into whom desires flow as rivers into the ocean, which though brimming with water remains ever the same; not he whom desire carries away.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 2.70 That man attains peace into whom all desires enter in the same way as the waters flow into a sea that remains unchanged (even) when being filled up from all sides. Not so one who is desirous of objects.

records.sanskrit:
विहाय कामान्यः सर्वान्पुमांश्चरति निःस्पृहः।
निर्ममो निरहङ्कारः स शान्तिमधिगच्छति ॥
records.iast:
vihāya kāmānyaḥ sarvānpumāṃścarati niḥspṛhaḥ
nirmamo nirahaṅkāraḥ sa śāntimadhigacchati
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
Yea! whoso, shaking off the yoke of flesh
  Lives lord, not servant, of his lusts; set free
  From pride, from passion, from the sin of "Self,"
  Toucheth tranquillity!

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 2.71 That man attains peace who, abandoning all desires, moves about without longing, without the sense of mine and without egoism.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 2.71 He attains Peace who, giving up desire, moves through the world without aspiration, possessing nothing which he can call his own, and free from pride.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 2.71 That man attains peace who, after rejecting all desires, moves about free from hankering, without the idea of ('me' and) 'mine', and devoid of pride.

records.sanskrit:
एषा ब्राह्मी स्थितिः पार्थ नैनां प्राप्य विमुह्यति।
स्थित्वास्यामन्तकालेऽपि ब्रह्मनिर्वाणमृच्छति ॥
records.iast:
eṣā brāhmī sthitiḥ pārtha naināṃ prāpya vimuhyati
sthitvāsyāmantakāle.api brahmanirvāṇamṛcchati
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
O Pritha's Son!
  That is the state of Brahm! There rests no dread
  When that last step is reached! Live where he will,
  Die when he may, such passeth from all 'plaining,
  To blest Nirvana, with the Gods, attaining.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 2.72 This is the Brahmic seat (eternal state), O son of Pritha. Attaining to this, none is deluded. Being established therein, even at the end of life, one attains to oneness with Brahman.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 2.72 O Arjuna! This is the state of the Self, the Supreme Spirit, to which if a man once attain, it shall never be taken from him. Even at the time of leaving the body, he will remain firmly enthroned there, and will become one with the Eternal."

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 2.72 O Partha, this is the state of being established in Brahman. One does not become deluded after attaining this. One attains identification with Brahman by being established in this state even in the closing years of one's life.
